title: WHO and UNICEF seek humanitarian pauses for a polio vaccination campaign in Gaza
body:
On 16 August 2024, the World Health Organization and UNICEF asked all parties to the conflict in Gaza to agree to seven-day humanitarian pauses so that two rounds of a polio vaccination campaign could be carried out, one at the end of August and one in September 2024. They said the campaign could not be delivered without the pauses.

On 16 July 2024, wastewater tests confirmed circulating variant type 2 poliovirus (cVDPV2) in six samples collected on 23 June from Khan Younis and Deir al-Balah. Sequencing linked the strain to a variant last detected in Egypt in 2023. Three children with suspected acute flaccid paralysis, a common symptom of polio, were reported, and their stool samples were sent to the Jordan National Polio Laboratory.

The campaign planned to give two drops of the nOPV2 vaccine in each round to more than 640,000 children under ten, using over 1.6 million doses, 708 vaccination teams and about 2,700 health workers. At least 95 percent coverage was needed in each round, with a four-week interval between doses.
